findings.title: Tight coupling to HTTP protocol
findings.description: All HTTP concerns are embedded directly in runner. Changing protocol or adding retry logic would require modifying this file.
findings.suggestion: Extract HTTP communication into a separate package or interface (e.g., 'coordinator' package with CoordinatorClient interface).
findings.benefit: Easier to swap implementations (e.g., gRPC, local socket) and test in isolation.
findings.impact: Medium - affects long-term maintainability and testing.

findings.title: Logging mixed with business logic
findings.description: log package used directly throughout. No abstraction for logging makes testing harder and couples to log implementation.
findings.suggestion: Accept logger interface in Config: type Logger interface { Errorf, Infof, Debugf ... }
findings.benefit: Easier to add structured logging, metrics, or change logging implementation.
findings.impact: Low-Medium - more of a best practice than critical issue.

findings.title: Multiple HTTP endpoint concerns in one file
findings.description: Runner handles 3 different API endpoints (list jobs, update status, post results). Each has slightly different error handling.
findings.suggestion: Consider moving HTTP concerns to separate 'API client' layer or package.
findings.impact: Low - current organization is acceptable for single-file service.

findings.title: No error recovery strategy between retries
findings.description: When job processing fails, runner moves to next poll interval. No exponential backoff or circuit breaker for repeated failures.
findings.currentBehavior: Failures are logged and ignored, next poll happens after fixed PollInterval.
findings.riskScenario: If coordinator is down for extended period, agent continuously polls without any backoff.
findings.suggestion: Consider exponential backoff or circuit breaker pattern for repeated API failures.
findings.impact: Low - acceptable for current use case, but improves resilience.

findings.title: Job completion semantics embedded in runner
findings.description: The decision to mark job as 'completed' or 'failed' based on exit code is hardcoded. If semantics change, code must be modified.
findings.suggestion: Consider moving this logic to Job struct or a separate strategy function.
findings.impact: Very low - semantics unlikely to change.
